learning_outcomes.text: Know and apply CAD/CAM/CAE tools to manufacturing processes by forming, plastic deformation, and material removal.
Know and apply automatic prototyping techniques.
Be able to design automated manufacturing processes based on CAD/CAM/CAE environments.
Be able to perform tests and trials in the manufacturing laboratory, in CAD/CAM environments, analyzing results and drawing conclusions.
Is able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Simulation, analysis and calculation of manufacturing processes by forming, plastic deformation, and material removal
Topic 2: Automation of manufacturing processes and NC programming
assessment_rules: The final grade is weighted 35% for the exam grade and 65% for the laboratory grade. The laboratory grade is the average of 9 compulsory laboratory practices, each requiring a report. The exam grade is the average of two exams covering topics 1-2 and 3-4 respectively. A laboratory grade of 5 or higher is retained; otherwise, the student must take an exam for the laboratory part in the final exam. The exam grade is not retained, and students failing continuous assessment must take a final exam covering all material.
